real_qa.q: What are the three main types of skin cancer in Queensland?
real_qa.r: Queensland has the highest rate of skin cancers in the world. The most common type is basal cell carcinoma, typically appearing as a shiny nodule on the head and neck area. The second most common is squamous cell cancer, which presents as crusty raised plaques in sun-exposed areas. Melanoma is less common but more serious and aggressive, behaving very differently from the other two types.

real_qa.q: How often should someone in Queensland get a skin cancer check?
real_qa.r: In Queensland, most patients are encouraged to have an annual skin check with their GP or dermatologist. However, those with a heavy burden of skin cancer history, significant family history, genetic conditions, compromised immune systems, or who work outdoors should be more vigilant and get checked every 6 months rather than annually.

real_qa.q: What sun protection methods does Icon Cancer Centre Toowoomba recommend for skin cancer prevention?
real_qa.r: Dr. Kumar recommends the slip, slop, slap approach: slip into lightweight, fully clothed shirts and long pants when outdoors; slop on sunscreen of SPF 50 and above, paying special attention to forgotten areas like behind the ears, feet, and neck; and slap on a wide brim hat for more coverage than a cap. Additionally, seek shade between 10am and 3pm when UV index is highest, avoid reflective surfaces like sand or concrete, and wear UV-rated sunglasses.
real_qa.requete: slip slop slap sun protection skin cancer

real_qa.q: What are the main risk factors for developing head and neck cancer?
real_qa.r: The primary risk factors include heavy smoking history with cannabis or tobacco, heavy alcohol use beyond recommended levels, human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, poor dental hygiene and neglected oral ulcers. HPV is increasingly seen in younger patients who are not heavy smokers or drinkers but have contracted the virus, which can present as head and neck cancer.
real_qa.requete: risk factors head neck cancer smoking alcohol HPV

real_qa.q: What radiation therapy techniques does Icon Cancer Centre Toowoomba use for head and neck cancer?
real_qa.r: Icon Cancer Centre Toowoomba primarily uses volumetric arc therapy (VMAT), a highly specialized radiation technique designed to target tumor sites while sparing organs at risk and important structures in the head and neck to limit short and long-term side effects. They also offer intensity modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) less frequently, and stereotactic guided radiation therapy, though evidence for the latter in head and neck cancer is limited.
